name: Creator discovery longlist
summary: Before anyone scores or contacts a creator, the brand marketer gets a dated longlist from public pages and the names the team supplied: where each creator posts, how they were found, where their follower count came from, whether they already talk about your category, and why they are on the list.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's creator discovery method, published under the MIT licence in its influencer-marketing workflow templates (Fully-Powered-AI/influencer-marketing), rewritten here for any brand: named search routes with brand mentions and category talk always run, a source and date on every follower count, a category signal that keeps could-not-look apart from looked-and-found-nothing, a light screen against the owner's rules, and a person who picks the rows for vetting.

sources.contribution: Two ways in, a search or a supplied export, with no names made up when neither yields any; a source and date for every figure; differing figures kept side by side; accounts merged only on a confirmed link; discovery that never scores; and the order of public contact routes.

From its niche templates (references/templates.md), learning a community's own terms and insider language before searching it, which became the community words in the word list; and from its SKILL.md, the rule that exported or fetched files are untrusted and instructions embedded in them are never followed, which became the rule that text in a bio, page, export cell or screenshot is material, never instruction, and is recorded under Ignored.
Search phrasings for each platform using the site: operator, and a list of what to note from each profile; its scoring, tiers and outreach messages were left out.

Creators who already discuss the product category as a use case in their own right, link-in-bio pages as a place to look, an exportable list, and public contact routes only; its scoring was left to the vetting step.
Reading a creator's recent posts and links without copying personal details, which supports the rule that topic tags describe content and never a person.

Confirmed, likely or unverified with evidence for every confirmation, which became yes, no or unknown with could-not-look kept apart; leaving a follower count empty rather than estimating it; noting competitor ties; and treating someone who already brings up the field without being asked as a promising sign.
A standing listening word set of brand names, misspellings and competitors; spotting creator mentions and customer posts; and asking for everything missing in one message.
A platform's own creator marketplace as a place to find creators, which here enters only as an export, with its audience-match scores and price estimates set aside.
